origin.description: Style the digits of a number, either all in grey or with negatives in red.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: The values to style. Numbers are written with as.character when the result has to be text.

arguments.name: negative
arguments.text: Logical vector. TRUE marks a negative value. The result has this length, and x is repeated or cut to match it.

origin.details: pillar.subtle_num defaults to false. When it is true, the whole of x goes through style_subtle and negative is ignored. Otherwise the call is ifelse(negative, style_neg(x), x). A length-1 false does not run style_neg, so a number stays a number. A true anywhere makes the whole result character. as.character of a missing number stays missing. paste, used by the red style, writes that same missing number as the letters NA. 0.01, 0.02, and 0.03 keep those spellings.
origin.value: Text when any selected value was styled, otherwise the original values.

translation.description: The same choice. None is missing. A string result is one element and a list result is the vector.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A number, a string, None, or a list of those. Doubles are written with R's as.character.

arguments.name: negative
arguments.text: A bool, 0 or 1, None, or a list of those. The result follows this length. Zero is false and NaN is missing.

translation.details: pillar.subtle_num defaults to false. When it is true, style_subtle runs on x and the shape follows x. Otherwise this is ifelse. Both arms run only when negative contains both true and false. All false leaves numbers as numbers. A true makes every element text, and the values that are not negative use as.character, which keeps a missing value missing. Set cli.num_colors first.
translation.value: A string or number when negative is a single value, or a list when negative is a list. With pillar.subtle_num true, the shape follows x.
translation.example:
from cli._options import options as cli_options

cli_options(**{"cli.num_colors": 8})

from pillar.styles import style_subtle_num

print(style_subtle_num([0.01 * i for i in (1, 2, 3)], [True, False, True]))
